title: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan attends public reception in Shillong; lays foundation stones for projects worth over ₹1,000 crore
subtitle:
Every State, village and citizen must become ‘Viksit’ to realise Viksit Bharat by 2047: Vice-President

Vice-President recalls former Lok Sabha colleague late P. A. Sangma as a great leader and Parliamentarian
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 SEP 2026 7:25PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today attended a public reception organised in his honour by the people and Government of Meghalaya at Soso Tham Auditorium, Shillong. He expressed gratitude for the warm welcome and said he would always stand with the people of Meghalaya in the State’s development journey.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced a public reception organised in his honour by the people and Government of Meghalaya at Soso Tham Auditorium, Shillong today.
The Vice President laid the foundation stones for five projects worth over ₹1000 crores. These include…
pic.twitter.com/OZqJPC1g2Y
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
September 7, 2026
The Vice-President highlighted Meghalaya’s rich cultural heritage, natural beauty and unique social institutions, including its matrilineal heritage. He said the State’s vibrant grassroots institutions reflect India’s diversity and democratic traditions. Recalling his former Lok Sabha colleague, late Shri P. A. Sangma, he described him as a great leader and an outstanding speaker who made a significant contribution to parliamentary democracy.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said true secularism means respecting each other’s thoughts an beliefs. He emphasised that people must live together with mutual respect and harmony. He also stressed that development must be inclusive and no section of society should be left behind.
Highlighting the importance of connectivity, the Vice-President said every effort is being made to connect remote villages with towns and cities. He noted that over 46,000 km of rural roads have been constructed in the North-East under PMGSY in the last decade, with expenditure of over ₹47,000 crore. He also appreciated Meghalaya’s reform-linked MoU under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.
The Vice President laid the foundation stones for five projects worth ₹1,010.95 crore. These include the New Shillong Water Supply Scheme Phase II, Part A (₹850.58 crore) under the Urban Challenge Fund, two road connectivity projects under NESIDS, a 30-bedded AYUSH facility at Shillong Civil Hospital and a 132/33 KV substation at Mawkhanu under PM-DevINE.
He also inaugurated the Maternity and Children’s Hospital at Nongstoin, completed at a cost of ₹31.05 crore under the National Health Mission. He said the projects, together worth about ₹1,042 crore, will strengthen water supply, connectivity, healthcare and power infrastructure in Meghalaya.
The Vice-President appreciated the State Government’s initiatives in infrastructure and tourism, including the homestay programme, CM-Elevate and Green Meghalaya. He congratulated Chief Minister Shri Conrad K. Sangma, his Council of Ministers and the people of Meghalaya for the State’s progress.
Speaking on the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan emphasised that progress must be inclusive, leaving no section of society behind, while preserving Meghalaya’s rich environment, culture and traditions. Referring to the State’s living-root bridges and the landscapes of Sohra and Mawsynram, he said Meghalaya offers valuable lessons in living in harmony with nature.
Chief Minister Shri Conrad K. Sangma, Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Prestone Tynsong and Shri Sniawbhalang Dhar, Minister Shri Sanbor Shullai, Chief Secretary Dr. Shakil P. Ahammed and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

title: Vice-President lays foundation stone for ₹110 crore infrastructure projects at Gauhati University
subtitle:
Vice President Releases books on Bhupen Hazarika and Assamese lexicography at Gauhati University

Assamese-Tamil literary translations reflect India’s cultural unity: Vice-President

Say No to Drugs, manage time wisely and stay disciplined: Vice-President to youth

Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision has expanded higher education opportunities across Bharat: Vice-President

Vice-President lauds Assam’s progress in education, infrastructure and employment
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 SEP 2026 2:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today laid the foundation stone for ₹110 crore infrastructure development projects at Gauhati University, including a new multidisciplinary academic building, a new boys’ and international students’ hostel, and works related to the auditorium and library.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan laid the foundation stone for ₹110 crore infrastructure development projects at Gauhati University today.
The Vice President welcomed the translation of Assamese and Tamil literary works into each other and encouraged greater academic…
pic.twitter.com/2DpbpgiZeW
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
September 7, 2026
Addressing the gathering, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan highlighted the historic significance of Gauhati University, established on January 26, 1948, as the first university in Northeast India, following a sustained public movement led by eminent leaders including Bharat Ratna Gopinath Bordoloi. He noted that the University has grown into a premier institution in the region, with NAAC A+ accreditation and 9th rank among State Public Universities in NIRF 2025.
Appreciating the University’s efforts to preserve India’s linguistic heritage, he said language carries the memory, wisdom and identity of a civilisation. He welcomed the translation of Assamese and Tamil literary works into each other and encouraged greater academic and literary exchanges between Assam and Tamil Nadu, observing that India’s linguistic diversity is enriched by its cultural unity.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan appreciated the University’s research on the Brahmaputra Basin, endangered languages, multilingualism, women’s studies, environmental sustainability and Indian Knowledge Systems. Describing the Brahmaputra as an ecological, economic and civilisational force, he stressed the importance of research addressing both regional and national challenges.
Highlighting the expansion of India’s higher education ecosystem since 2014, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan lauded the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in expanding educational opportunities across the country, noting the establishment of new IITs, IIMs, IIITs, Central Universities, AIIMS and other institutions. He also highlighted the 42.2 per cent rise in women’s enrolment in higher education, from 1.57 crore in 2014-15 to 2.24 crore in 2023-24, describing women’s increasing participation and academic achievements as a significant indicator of empowerment.
He appreciated Assam’s development trajectory under the leadership of Chief Minister Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma, particularly in infrastructure, connectivity, education, investment and employment. He highlighted the State’s improved education performance, the commencement of the first MBA batch at IIM Guwahati and more than 1.64 lakh merit-based government appointments since 2021.
Calling upon students and scholars to contribute to Viksit Bharat @2047, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan urged them to dream boldly, pursue research addressing community challenges, ensure technology serves humanity and make innovation a vehicle for inclusive development. Quoting Swami Vivekananda, he urged the youth to “Awake, arise and stop not till your goal is reached.”
On the occasion, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan released Bhupen Hazarika: Hundred Years of a Wandering Songs, edited by Ankuran Dutta and Nani Gopal Mahanta, and the 5th revised and enlarged edition of Chandrakanta Abhidhan.
The Vice-President also witnessed a cultural programme presented by Gauhati University students, showcasing Assam’s rich cultural heritage. He also led students and other participants in taking the “No to Drugs” pledge, urging young people to stay away from substance abuse, exercise self-discipline, manage their time wisely and limit excessive social media use.
The programme was attended by Governor of Assam Shri Lakshman Prasad Acharya, Chief Minister Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma, Education Minister Dr. Ranoj Pegu, Chief Secretary Dr. Ravi Kota, Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University Shri Nani Gopal Mahanta, Registrar Prof. Utpal Sarma, faculty members, students and other dignitaries.

title: THIRTY-THREE PER CENT RESERVATION WILL OPEN NEW AVENUES FOR WOMEN’S POLITICAL LEADERSHIP: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
subtitle:
THE DAY IS NOT FAR WHEN WOMEN WILL ACCOUNT FOR OVER 50 PERCENT OF PUBLIC SERVICES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

FOCUS MUST SHIFT FROM MERELY PROVIDING SUPPORT TO EMPOWERING WOMEN TO SHAPE POLICIES AND LAWS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

INDIA CANNOT PROGRESS TOWARDS A DEVELOPED NATION WITHOUT THE ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LOK SABHA SPEAKER INAUGURATES A TWO-DAY ALL-INDIA CAPACITY BUILDING WORKSHOP ON "GENDER-RESPONSIVE GOVERNANCE" ORGANIZED BY THE NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR WOMEN (NCW) IN FARIDABAD
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 SEP 2026 6:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today highlighted the significance of greater representation of women in democratic institutions, referring to the provision of 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies as a historic need. Observing the growing presence of women across various public services and professions, Shri Birla said that the coming years would witness a new generation of women leaders emerging across political, administrative, and social spheres. He added that the day is not far when women will account for over 50 percent of public services.
Shri Birla made these observations while inaugurating a two-day All-India Capacity Building Workshop on the theme "Gender-Responsive Governance," organized by the National Commission for Women (NCW) in Faridabad today.
Mentioning that the focus must now shift from merely providing support and opportunities to women towards enabling them to actively shape policies, programmes, and laws, Shri Birla stressed that women should themselves participate in determining the legislation required to address their concerns and aspirations. Referring to the constitutional commitment to equality and various legislative measures undertaken for women’s safety, empowerment, and self-reliance, he highlighted that institutions such as the NCW have an important role in identifying emerging challenges and facilitating solutions. He emphasized that women legislators—through the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, Panchayats, and Municipalities—can play a decisive role in bringing women's concerns before appropriate fora and ensuring that laws respond to ground-level realities.
Shri Birla also stressed that India cannot progress toward the goal of a developed nation without the economic and social empowerment of its women, who constitute nearly half of the country’s population. Every woman, he said, should have opportunities for employment, economic independence, and social empowerment. He called upon women legislators to deliberate on effective policies, schemes, and legislative measures that can strengthen women economically and socially, particularly those facing deprivation and hardship. The experiences and successful initiatives of different legislatures, he suggested, should be shared so that best practices can be replicated nationwide. Furthermore, he underlined the need to enhance awareness among women about the laws and institutional mechanisms available to address their concerns, particularly in vulnerable areas.
Noting that women have always been at the forefront of India’s transformation—from the freedom movement and nation-building to strengthening democratic institutions—Shri Birla emphasized that the programme provides an essential platform for women legislators to exchange experiences, ideas, and perspectives, thereby strengthening their leadership capabilities. The participation of women legislators from various States and Union Territories, he noted, demonstrates the significant role they play in giving voice to women's aspirations through legislative forums, and he urged participants to sharpen their skills to fulfill this mandate.
Emphasizing the importance of dialogue in a vibrant democracy, Shri Birla said that the challenges and aspirations of the people are best addressed through continuous discussion and consultation. He underlined that sensitivity is a core strength of women’s leadership, fostering a deeper understanding of people’s concerns and a greater capacity to find effective solutions. A sensitive and responsive work culture, he added, can contribute significantly to addressing social challenges and strengthening democratic institutions. Advancing women’s leadership, he concluded, must remain a collective resolve, expressing hope that sustained efforts will lead to women increasingly occupying leadership positions across every sphere of national life.
On this occasion,  Chairperson of the National Commission for Women, Smt. Vijaya Rahatkar; Shri Rajesh Nagar, Minister of State (IC) for Food, Civil Supplies & Consumer Affairs, Govt. of Haryana  and around 200 women legislators from 20 States and 2 Union Territories were present.

title: PM to Visit Gujarat and Maharashtra on 8th September
subtitle:
PM to Lay Foundation Stones, Inaugurate and Dedicate to the Nation Development Projects Worth More Than ₹35,000 Crore in Vadodara

PM to Dedicate Three Key Sections of Western Dedicated Freight Corridor to the Nation, Marking Completion of the Project

PM to Lay Foundation Stone for three Railway Projects and three Highway Projects

PM to Inaugurate Global Fintech Fest 2026 in Mumbai

Theme of GFF 2026: “Potential to Impact: Agentic AI, Tokenisation, Quantum - Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 SEP 2026 11:51AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will visit Gujarat and Maharashtra on 8th September 2026. At around 12 noon, Prime Minister will lay the foundation stones, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth more than ₹35,000 crore in Vadodara. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.
At around 5:45 PM, Prime Minister will inaugurate Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026 in Mumbai and address the gathering as well.
PM in Vadodara
Prime Minister will dedicate to the nation three important sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC), covering 326 route kilometres and developed at a cost of more than ₹20,700 crore. These include the New Sanand (N)- New Makarpura, New Umbergaon-New Saphale and New Saphale- New JNPT sections.
The direct connectivity of Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA) will facilitate faster movement of EXIM cargo, strengthen connectivity between industrial centres and ports, reduce logistics costs and help decongest Mumbai’s railway network.
With the commissioning of these sections, the Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC) network will stand fully operational across its entire length. The dedicated freight infrastructure will further strengthen the country’s logistics ecosystem by improving multimodal connectivity, reducing transit time and facilitating seamless movement of cargo across different regions.
Prime Minister will also flag off freight train services from New Sanand (North), New Makarpura, New Umbergaon and New JNPT, Mumbai. In addition, he will flag off a new passenger train service between Tanda Road and Vadodara (Pratapnagar).
Prime Minister will dedicate to the nation the Jobat–Tanda Road new rail line, developed as part of the Chhota Udepur–Dhar project. The new rail line will connect remote and tribal areas of Alirajpur with the national rail network.
Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone for three railway projects spanning 329 kilometres and costing more than ₹9,700 crore. These include the Vadodara-Ratlam third and fourth lines, Miyagam Karjan-Choranda–Malsar gauge conversion and the Vishwamitri-Dabhoi doubling project. The projects will enhance passenger and freight capacity, ease congestion and strengthen connectivity between Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.
Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone for three National Highway projects costing around ₹1,780 crore. These include six-laning of the Kamrej-Chalthan section of NH-48; construction of additional structures, including major bridges over the Tapi and Narmada, on the Vadodara-Surat section of NH-48; and grade-separated structures at Abhava, Mindhola and Khajod junctions on NH-53.
Prime Minister will also lay the foundation stone for and inaugurate various Government of Gujarat projects worth around ₹2,600 crore. Major projects for which the foundation stone will be laid include Vadodara Urban Development Authority Ring Road Phase II and a 110 MW floating solar project at Kadana Dam, construction of new office of Vadodara Municipal Corporation, among others. Projects to be inaugurated include housing projects under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) and a water-supply project for 11 villages in eastern Vadodara, among others.
PM in Mumbai
Prime Minister will inaugurate Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026, one of the world’s largest and most influential annual fintech conferences.
The seventh edition of the Global Fintech Fest is being held from 8th to 11th September 2026 in Mumbai. Since 2020, GFF has emerged as an international thought leadership platform bringing together policymakers, regulators, central banks, financial institutions, fintechs, technology companies, investors, academia and other global stakeholders to deliberate on shaping the future of finance.
The theme of GFF 2026 is “Potential to Impact: Agentic AI, Tokenisation, Quantum - Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance.”
GFF 2026 has been designed as a convergence point for policy, regulation, technology, capital and industry on a common platform. It seeks to build on India’s leadership in digital payments and financial inclusion and move from potential to impact. The discussions will focus on how Agentic AI, programmable finance, quantum technologies and other critical and emerging technologies can create trusted, inclusive and measurable outcomes for citizens, enterprises and economies globally.

title: 11th Ayurveda Day 2026 to be Celebrated in Nagpur, Maharashtra under the Theme “Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow”
subtitle:
From tradition to innovation, Ayurveda can shape a healthier tomorrow: Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav

Ayurveda Day 2026 to become a National Health Communication Campaign: Shri Prataprao Jadhav
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 SEP 2026 2:55PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (I/C) for Ayush and Union Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, addressed the Curtain Raiser Press Conference for the 11th Ayurveda Day 2026 at the National Media Centre, New Delhi. The event marked the commencement of the nationwide campaign leading up to Ayurveda Day.
The main Ayurveda Day celebrations will be held on 23 September 2026 in Nagpur, Maharashtra, with “Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow”
‘स्वस्थ भविष्य के लिए आयुर्वेद
’
as its theme, reflecting the vision of connecting India’s rich Ayurvedic heritage with the evolving healthcare needs of the future.
In his address, Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav highlighted that the world is increasingly looking towards preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles, nutrition, wellness and holistic health, areas where which India has a rich tradition and experience.  He emphasized that Ayurveda Day is not merely an occasion to celebrate India’s heritage, but an opportunity to connect this heritage with the health requirements of the future.
In line with the vision of Viksit Bharat under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Shri Prataprao Jadhav highlighted the need for a healthcare approach where health goes beyond treatment of disease and encompasses healthy habits, appropriate diet and daily routines, mental balance and harmony with nature.
Shri Prataprao Jadhav outlined three important areas that will guide this year’s Ayurveda Day campaign: “Integrative Healthcare for Better Health Outcomes,” with a focus on leveraging the expertise and strengths of different systems of medicine for better health outcomes; “Evidence, Research and Innovation in Ayurveda,” emphasizing research, evidence and innovation as essential pillars for the wider global acceptance and future development of Ayurveda; and “Ayurveda for Community Wellbeing and Sustainable Living,” highlighting the role of Ayurveda in promoting the wellbeing of individuals, families and communities while encouraging sustainable living.
Shri Jadhav emphasized the important role of the media in disseminating accurate, evidence-based and simple information on Ayurveda to the public. He noted that while Ayurveda enjoys widespread acceptance, it is important to address misconceptions and ensure that citizens have access to reliable information. He called upon the media to support the campaign and take the message of Ayurveda to homes, schools and colleges, young people including Gen Z, and rural and urban communities.  He emphasized that the 11th Ayurveda Day should go beyond being a government programme and evolve into a people’s movement and a national health communication campaign.
Calling for a stronger connection between India’s traditional knowledge and contemporary healthcare needs, Shri Jadhav said that the campaign should seek to connect tradition with knowledge, knowledge with evidence, evidence with innovation, and innovation with public welfare.
Prof. Sanjeev Sharma, Vice-Chancellor, National Institute of Ayurveda (NIA), Jaipur, highlighted the key features of Ayurveda Day 2026, which will focus on evidence-based Ayurveda, research and innovation, integrated healthcare, and community wellbeing and sustainable living. He also outlined the major programmes planned for the occasion, including the National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Awards 2026, along with key initiatives such as new programmes at NIA Jaipur, safety dossiers on medicinal plants, Standard Treatment Guidelines for skin diseases, a report on the Ayush Services Sector, and Ayush Vision 2030, besides exchange of MoUs and other activities.
The Curtain Raiser programme was also attended by Ms. Alarmelmangai D., Joint Secretary, Ministry of Ayush; Shri Satyajit Paul, DDG, Ministry of Ayush; Shri Dhirendra Ojha, Principal DG, PIB; senior officials of the Ministry of Ayush, Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS), All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), Delhi, National Institute of Ayurveda (NIA), Jaipur, and Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga (MDNIY); and representatives of the media, among others.
The Ministry of Ayush has called upon all stakeholders, including the media, Ayurveda practitioners, researchers, institutions and citizens, to actively participate in the nationwide campaign for the 11th Ayurveda Day 2026.

title: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan reviews action plan for strengthening KVKs through greater State participation
subtitle: Focus on upgradation of 300 KVKs by March 2027 and establishment of Incubation-cum-Skill Centres in all KVKs by December 2028
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 SEP 2026 3:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, today chaired a meeting in New Delhi to review the Action Plan for strengthening Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) through enhanced participation of States. The deliberations focused on the implementation of key recommendations concerning KVKs emerging from the 5th Chief Secretaries’ Conference 2025, and on measures to accelerate their implementation. Union Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, Shri Bhagirath Choudhary, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Dr. Mangi Lal Jat, and senior officials of the Ministry were present.
Discussions focused on the action point of upgrading the infrastructure and logistics of 300 prioritized KVKs by March 2027. Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan emphasized the need for active participation and timely support from State Governments to achieve the target within the stipulated timeframe. The Secretary, DARE, has engaged with the Chief Secretaries of all States and Union Territories to mobilize financial and institutional support for the upgradation of prioritized KVKs. Several States have initiated the process through their respective State Agricultural Universities. Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa and Chhattisgarh have
received
Detailed Project Reports (DPRs)
from Universities/KVKs
, while other States are at various stages of preparation and implementation.
Also covered the action point of establishing Incubation-cum-Skill Centres in all KVKs by December 2028. Under the initiative, KVKs are being mapped with agro-based enterprises, technical partner institutions and district-specific agricultural opportunities. KVK-wise incubation plans are being developed for submission to States and Union Territories for funding and implementation support.
Further detailed discussions
on
reforms concerning KVK personnel. The proposed reforms relating to pay, allowances and promotion of KVK staff have received approval from the Department of Expenditure (DoE). The role of State Governments in providing NPS contributions and retirement benefits for KVK staff, as applicable, was also emphasized. States were urged to undertake timely recruitment against vacancies to ensure adequate manpower for the effective functioning of KVKs and delivery of their mandated activities.
Attention was also drawn to the importance of ensuring timely release of funds to KVKs, particularly for seasonal agricultural programmes, so that planned activities are implemented within the appropriate agricultural window. Under the Cluster Frontline Demonstrations (CFLD) on Pulses and Oilseeds programme for 2026–27, activities are being implemented across 24 States through 353 KVKs/districts, with a target area of 12,349 hectares. An area of 9,750 hectares, has already been achieved. Issues relating to fund-flow mapping and delays in the release of funds in some States were discussed. States were requested to facilitate the smooth and timely flow of funds up to ATARI and KVK levels, ensure timely availability of recommended quality seeds and varieties, and strengthen coordination during the planning and execution of demonstrations.
Review also highlighted the role of KVKs in supporting the Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM DDKY). States were requested to provide adequate funding support to KVKs for implementing their mandated activities as well as district-specific action plans under PM DDKY. It was further emphasized that activities undertaken by KVKs at the district level, in addition to capacity-building programmes, should be captured and uploaded on the designated portal to facilitate comprehensive monitoring, reporting and assessment of outcomes.
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan emphasized that the transformation of KVKs requires strong Centre-State convergence, timely financial support, modern infrastructure, adequate manpower and effective implementation of district-specific action plans. He stressed the importance of ensuring that KVKs are equipped with the necessary infrastructure, human resources and institutional support to effectively serve the farming community and respond to emerging challenges in agriculture.
Strengthened KVKs will play a crucial role in taking scientific knowledge, modern agricultural technologies, improved varieties, skills, innovation and entrepreneurship opportunities closer to farmers and rural communities. The deliberations underscored the need for States and Union Territories to accelerate implementation of the agreed action points and strengthen convergence with the Centre and other stakeholders so that KVKs emerge as effective platforms for agricultural technology dissemination, skill development, innovation and rural entrepreneurship, thereby contributing to a developed and prosperous agricultural sector.

title: CIL Production, Power Sector Supplies Pick Up Sharply as Rains Recede
subtitle:
Daily Average Production Rises 35% from 1.36 MT during September 1–3 to 1.83 MT on September 6, 2026

Power sector dispatch up 24% improves from 1.37 MT to 1.7 MT
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 SEP 2026 5:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Coal India Limited (CIL) has witnessed a sharp improvement in coal production and supplies to the power sector with rainfall receding across its mining regions.
CIL’s average daily coal production, rose by 35%, which was around 1.36 Million Tonne (MT) during the first three rain-affected days of September, to approximately 1.83 MT on 6th September 2026. The improvement comes as mining conditions steadily recover and affected transportation routes and working areas are restored. The rise in production was led by CIL’s subsidiaries. During the same period, average daily production increased around 61% from 0.18 MT to 0.29 MT at NCL, up by 33% from 0.15 MT to 0.20 MT at SECL.
The improvement in production is translating into higher dispatches, with the power sector witnessing a clear pick-up in coal supplies. The average daily despatch to the power sector increased by 24% from around 1.37 MT during the first three days of September to 1.7 MT as on 6th September 2026. During the same period, power-sector dispatch increased by 56% from 0.18 MT to 0.28 MT at NCL, up 23% from 0.30 MT to 0.37 MT at SECL.
The improvement in production is being backed by a substantial increase in Overburden Removal (OBR), an important indicator of coal exposure and future production readiness. Average daily OBR doubled from 2.5 Million Cubic Metres (MCuM) during the first three days of September to 5.1 MCM on 6th September, 2026. OBR increased fourfold at NCL, over three times at SECL during the same period.
Resources have been reappropriated and remobilised to full deployment strength to accelerate overburden removal and expose additional coal.
The lower-horizon coal seams are steadily being brought back into operation through continuous dewatering. Mines that had been operating under geotechnical constraints during the monsoon are now opening up as the mine landscape widens with the return of dry spells.
One significant improvement is the availability of dry working benches and dry raw coal. With reduced moisture and stickiness, the coal acquires better free-flowing characteristics, facilitating smoother handling and conveyance.
CIL is taking additional measures to strengthen supplies to power plants, particularly critical plants drawing coal through Washery and RCR mode. Coal is being offered beyond the Monthly scheduled Quantity (MSQ) to interested Central and State Gencos and IPPs for road-mode lifting. Lifting of coal against Delivery Orders issued to critical power plants in road mode is also being prioritised.
The improvement in coal movement is visible across several mining areas.
Haul roads and coal transportation routes affected by heavy rainfall are being strengthened on a continuous basis across all mines of CIL. The impact of these measures became evident with the reduction in rainfall from September 3 onwards.
With production, overburden removal and power-sector dispatch all showing a strong upward movement, CIL is focusing on consolidating the recovery and further strengthening coal supplies.
The improving trend in September provides a positive outlook for CIL’s production and dispatch, with supplies to power plants gradually moving towards pre-monsoon levels.

title: DGFT Introduces Open API Facility for Certificate of Origin on the Trade Connect e-Platform
subtitle:
Exporters Can Now Apply for Certificates of Origin Directly from Their Own ERP or Accounting Software

Facility Covers Both Preferential and Non-Preferential Certificates of Origin
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 SEP 2026 4:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, has introduced an Open Application Programming Interface (API) facility for the issuance and verification of Certificates of Origin (CoO) through the Trade Connect e-Platform. The facility is now available for use by eligible exporters and their systems.
The Open API facility enables exporters to integrate their Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), accounting or other business software directly with the DGFT’s CoO system. At present, exporters are required to enter CoO-related details separately on the DGFT platform, even when the same information is already available in their business software. The new facility enables electronic transfer of application data from the exporter’s system to the DGFT platform, thereby eliminating repetitive data entry, reducing errors and expediting the application process.
The facility supports both Preferential and Non-Preferential Certificates of Origin. Preferential CoOs are issued under Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), Regional Trade Agreements (RTAs) and Preferential Trade Agreements (PTAs), enabling exporters to claim applicable tariff concessions in the importing country. Non-Preferential CoOs are issued for customs clearance, compliance, trade remedy and other trade purposes without providing tariff benefits.
Under the facility, exporters can obtain API credentials through the API Management section of the CoO Portal and register the IP addresses from which their systems will connect. Three APIs have been made available, namely the Authentication Token API for secure login, the CoO File API for submission of applications and receipt of certificates, and the Certificate Verification API for verification of issued certificates.
A transaction ledger is maintained for each application, providing details of the status of the application, including Draft, In Process, Approved, Certificate Issued and Rejected. The ledger also captures the acknowledgement ID, file number, file date and certificate number, enabling exporters to track their applications electronically.
The Open API facility incorporates multiple security safeguards to ensure secure and reliable exchange of information. All requests and responses are digitally signed using SHA-256 RSA digital signatures with 2048-bit X.509 certificates to ensure data integrity, authentication of the sender and non-repudiation. Passwords are protected using PBKDF2 hashing with a dynamic salt, while access is restricted to IP addresses whitelisted by the exporter. Each access token remains valid for 60 minutes.
The framework covers major trade agreements and certification schemes, including India–Japan CEPA, India–Korea CEPA, SAFTA, SAPTA, ASEAN–India FTA, India–Singapore CECA, India–Malaysia CECA, India–Chile PTA, India–Mercosur PTA, India–UAE CEPA, India–Australia ECTA, India–Oman CEPA, India–EFTA TEPA, India–UK CETA, the Generalized System of Preferences and the Non-Preferential CoO Scheme. The system automatically applies the relevant fields, origin criteria and validation rules based on the agreement or certification scheme selected by the exporter.
The registration, authentication and technical integration process is available on the Trade Connect e-Platform:
https://www.trade.gov.in/pages/certificate-of-origin
A step-by-step help manual has also been annexed to the Trade Notice.
Exporters, Export Promotion Councils, designated CoO issuing agencies and trade bodies may contact the DGFT Helpdesk through the toll-free numbers or e-mail for queries, suggestions and feedback relating to the eCoO module.
Further details are available in Trade Notice No. 25/2026-27 dated 07 September 2026, issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade.

title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for India to Emerge as a Global Medical and Healthcare Destination
subtitle:
India’s FTA Network Expands Market Access Opportunities for Healthcare Industry: Shri Goyal

India Must Strengthen Medtech Innovation, Incubation and Intellectual Property Ecosystem: Shri Goyal
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 SEP 2026 2:46PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal called for India to build on its position as the ‘pharmacy of the world’ and emerge as a global medical and healthcare destination. Addressing the Pharma Machtech and Labnext Expo 2026 in New Delhi, Shri Goyal highlighted the growing importance of healthcare beyond treatment, encompassing prevention, wellness, caregiving, diagnostics, laboratory capacities, medical devices, telemedicine, teleconsultation, digital health solutions, innovation and research and development for newer drugs and modern equipment.
The Minister also urged the industry to utilise the opportunities arising from India’s free trade agreements. He noted that prior to 2014, India’s free trade agreements collectively covered economies with a GDP of around $10 trillion, while the nine free trade and bilateral trade agreements finalised in the last four to four-and-a-half years cover economies with a combined GDP of around $60 trillion. He said ongoing negotiations could further expand this coverage to around $75 trillion, providing opportunities for preferential lower-duty market access, services and mobility.
Shri Goyal highlighted that the government has created new opportunities for the youth and strengthened India’s position as a trusted international partner. He called upon stakeholders to participate in the country’s development journey and work towards ensuring access to quality education, healthcare and opportunities for all.
He said the medical and pharmaceutical machinery, consumables and related sectors represent a growing field with significant potential for merchandise exports, import substitution and services exports. He said the healthcare ecosystem has the potential to create crores of jobs, thousands of business opportunities and lakhs of new startups, particularly in the medtech field. He noted that the sector can create business opportunities, jobs and income for young people while contributing to the availability of quality healthcare across the country.
The Minister called for strengthening the startup incubation ecosystem for medtech, medical equipment and consumables, along with improvements in design, copyrights, patent laws and the intellectual property ecosystem. He encouraged collaboration with R&D centres in other countries, inviting global innovators and large pharmaceutical companies to India and setting up design centres in the country.
Shri Goyal called for technology partnerships, stronger buyer-seller relationships and joint ventures to advance self-reliance in the sector. He emphasised that India need not reinvent the wheel and can bring suitable global technologies to India while taking Indian technologies to global markets. He also encouraged co-designing, co-developing, licensing, knowledge sharing and knowledge transfer.
The Minister emphasised the need for self-reliance in research, medicines and medical equipment and said Export Promotion Councils and industry stakeholders have an important role to play in this endeavour. He noted that the Goods and Services Tax (GST) has been amended to improve affordability and opportunities for the sector. He also highlighted the commitment of ₹1 lakh crore towards research and development, innovation and funding, and urged stakeholders to leverage these opportunities to develop newer equipment, innovative drugs and medicines.
Shri Goyal emphasised the need to strengthen resilience in healthcare supply chains through greater indigenisation of equipment. Recalling the experience during COVID-19, including shortages of oxygenators and ventilators, he stressed the importance of learning from the experience and ensuring high quality with zero compromise on standards.
The Minister said India should aim not only to provide high-quality healthcare to every Indian but also to provide wellness and healthcare services to the world from India. He highlighted the potential of an integrated healthcare ecosystem comprising Indian medical equipment and pharmaceuticals, patient care by Indian doctors, nursing and caregiving, technicians, hospital administrators, management personnel and engineering staff.
Shri Goyal also noted that Artificial Intelligence would bring greater efficiency and support healthcare professionals to perform their work better, smarter and faster, while human caregiving and nursing would continue to remain essential.
The Minister highlighted India’s cost advantage in research and development and said greater collaboration among industry, academia, medical colleges, IITs and other centres of excellence can significantly expand the scale of research and development. He highlighted the potential for innovation, design and clinical trials in India, along with manufacturing equipment in the country.
Shri Goyal said 100 per cent Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) is permitted through the automatic route. Referring to the Economic Survey 2025–26, he noted that the pharmaceutical industry is shifting from volume to value.
He called for strengthening the critical component ecosystem and domestic capabilities through high-quality equipment, with zero compromise on quality. He proposed the creation of shared testing infrastructure and facilities where Indian equipment can be tested, benchmarked against the best in the world, certified and demonstrated to global customers. He said the government of India would support the acquisition of the best technical testing equipment for such facilities in government-sponsored or university laboratories.
The Minister expressed confidence that the collective efforts of industry, entrepreneurs, startups, researchers, healthcare professionals and other stakeholders can contribute to India’s journey towards becoming a developed nation by 2047.

title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Trained Caregivers and Wider Hospital Participation in Heal in India Gateway
subtitle:
Shri Goyal Underscores the Importance of Seamless Patient Journeys, Global Promotion of Indian Healthcare and Quality-Focused Expansion Across States

India Should Target 10 Million Medical Value Tourists Annually: Shri Goyal

India’s Clinical Excellence, Advanced Technologies and 60–80% Lower Healthcare Costs Offer Huge Potential to Serve the World

Shri Goyal Stresses Quality, Professional Integrity and Zero Tolerance for Corruption in Healthcare Certification
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 SEP 2026 2:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today outlined a five-point action plan to strengthen India’s medical value tourism ecosystem and position the country as a gateway for international health and wellness services with the highest quality standards. Addressing the inaugural ceremony of Sanjeevani 2026 at Bharat Health Global Expo 2026 in New Delhi, Shri Goyal said the first priority should be to train and certify caregivers and develop a skilled workforce capable of providing healthcare of international standards.
The second point, he said, should be to encourage more hospitals to join the Heal in India gateway and publish honest and transparent treatment packages. He stressed that hospitals must follow ethical practices and never attempt to cheat patients, as one wrong action can lead to loss of goodwill, business and credibility for India.
As the third point, Shri Goyal called upon insurers and health-tech companies to build products and platforms that make the patient journey more seamless, ensuring timely reimbursements and greater availability of cashless payments. He also suggested that teleconsultations and telemedicine could be incorporated in a big way as an initial part of the medical value tourism journey.
The fourth point was the need to organise exhibitions and presentations across the world, establish facilitators and tie-ups with hospitals globally, and ensure that only National Accreditation Board for Hospitals & Healthcare Providers
(NABH)-enabled, verified and panelled hospitals are allowed to treat patients coming from abroad. He stressed that NABH must maintain the highest standards with zero compromise.
As the fifth point, the Minister urged States to focus on quality in hospitals and wellness centres, expand their networks, make good-quality facilities globally visible and market these facilities for the welfare of patients. He called for medical value tourism to expand beyond metropolitan cities to Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, creating jobs, opportunities and infrastructure while also helping upgrade healthcare for Indian patients.
Shri Goyal also suggested creating a pool of interpreters for patients arriving from different countries and speaking different languages, so that they have greater confidence and communication between patients and the medical system becomes easier.
The Minister emphasised that quality healthcare cannot be different for Indians and foreigners. He said India must ensure that every Indian patient receives the same high-quality healthcare as anyone coming from across the world. He said the country must give to its brothers and sisters what it would wish to receive itself and provide the same quality of healthcare to every person from India or abroad, without discrimination between rich and poor.
Shri Goyal stressed that those who entrust their lives to India by coming here for treatment must be treated with the highest care, concern and compassion. He said patients travelling abroad for healthcare, whether from Africa, Asia, America or Europe, experience anxiety as they enter a new country and seek clarity, dignity, ethical best practices and high integrity. They place their trust in India at every stage of their healthcare journey.
Highlighting the potential of India’s medical value tourism sector, Shri Goyal said India has clinical excellence, advanced technologies and healthcare costs 60-80 per cent lower than in other parts of the world, particularly the developed world. He said India also has compassion in abundance and appreciated the care and concern demonstrated by medical professionals across the country, from small nursing homes and doctors’ clinics to large municipal, private and government hospitals, often while working under considerable constraints.
The Minister said India’s pharmaceutical industry, medtech sector, diagnostics, traditional medicines including Ayurveda, Yoga and Unani, doctors, technicians, nurses, caregivers and hospitals collectively constitute the country’s strength and can make medical value tourism a potent instrument for serving the world. He said the sector has the potential to take India to the world, earn goodwill and serve people globally while creating a huge number of jobs and business opportunities in the manufacture of drugs, medical equipment and consumables, delivery of these products, hospital infrastructure and employment for doctors, teachers, nurses, technicians and other professionals.
Shri Goyal said that while 3.5 million patients have benefited from India’s medical value tourism ecosystem in the last seven years, the country’s target should be 10 million patients a year. He said India has the ability, capability, right doctors and the right ecosystem to achieve this. He emphasised that high standards, ethics, integrity and honesty must be maintained and urged healthcare providers to go the extra mile in caring for international patients.
Referring to the changing global healthcare landscape, Shri Goyal said the world is ageing while India is young and that many new-age diseases are spreading across the world. Healthcare costs are increasing and many parts of the world face long waiting lists even for doctors’, dentists’ and radiologists’ appointments, along with shortages of tertiary care. He said countries with which India is engaging through FTAs and business discussions want high-quality pharmaceuticals, doctors, technicians, nurses and caregivers from India in large numbers.
The Minister underlined the importance of preventive healthcare and the wellness ecosystem, referring to Ayurveda in Kerala and its spread across the country, wellness centres in the hills, and the care provided by nurses and young men and women working in the healthcare system. He said India is the land which can serve best and urged stakeholders not to miss the opportunity presented by the medical value tourism sector.
Emphasising collaboration, Shri Goyal said the purpose of Bharat Health was to bring the entire fragmented healthcare sector together and called upon stakeholders to work as collaborators and in cooperation with each other as a team.  Shri Goyal said the healthcare sector is a perfect example of the need for collaboration and cooperation, as even a small error can have serious consequences.
He said India must maintain high-quality benchmarks and make quality visible to patients. He called for the scaling up of medical value tourism while maintaining high standards and said India should become the gateway for international health and wellness services with the highest quality standards available anywhere in the world.
Shri Goyal said the world is looking to India for high-quality pharmaceuticals, doctors, technicians, nurses and caregivers, and that India has the potential to respond to this demand. He reiterated that the sector presents an opportunity to serve the world while creating economic opportunities and societal benefits.
On healthcare for Indians, Shri Goyal highlighted Ayushman Bharat, under which poor people and their families do not have to worry about healthcare expenses when someone falls sick, as the government pays for their healthcare. He also highlighted the provision for all persons above 70 years of age, irrespective of income, to receive an additional healthcare cover of ₹5 lakh.
Shri Goyal said India’s approach to healthcare has always been guided by the principle of serving the world. Referring to the Upanishadic expression “Sarvesantu Niramaya”, meaning “may all beings be free from illness”, he said India has never viewed healthcare only within the boundaries of the country and has for thousands of years regarded healthcare as a shared responsibility of the entire world. He described “One World, One Health” as part of this basic ethos.
Recalling India’s response during the COVID period, Shri Goyal said India provided vaccines free of charge to countries that could not afford them and supplied vaccines to others at very low cost. While vaccines from the developed world were sold for around 25-30 dollars, Indian vaccines were available at around 2-3 dollars a dose. Shri Goyal stressed that India never profiteered at the cost of somebody else’s misery.
The Minister recalled that when medicines required during COVID were available in India, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi decided to impose export restrictions on medicines being used at that time. He said that although very few medicines were proven for the treatment of COVID, paracetamol, certain other medicines, injections, injectables and consumables were required. He explained that export controls were introduced to safeguard India’s stock of medicines from being purchased or cornered by unscrupulous traders, certain companies or rich nations. Otherwise, only the rich could have received treatment while poorer and less-privileged populations, developing countries and India’s poor and lower-middle-class population could have been deprived of these medicines.
Shri Goyal said India not only ensured that everyone in the country who needed medicines received them, but also ensured equitable distribution of available medicines and equipment to countries across the world, whether rich or poor. More than 100 countries received medicines free of charge. He stressed that India did not profiteer from what it had and shared resources with others either free of charge or at cost.
Calling this the ethos of India, Shri Goyal said the third edition of Sanjeevani is bringing to the fore the potential contribution India can make to serve the country and the world. He said India must continue to ensure that healthcare for its own people is not compromised and referred to the various ways in which quality and timely healthcare are being made available.
The Minister also emphasised the importance of quality, ethics and integrity in the healthcare ecosystem. He said quality will determine the future of India and described the Quality Council of India as one of the most important organisations if India is to become a developed nation by 2047. He said maintaining high standards would be central to India’s future.
Shri Goyal stressed the importance of professional integrity in certification and said that the NABH system should be professionally run and free from influence. He stated that the Ministry or Government has not referred a single case and that the system is professionally managed. He urged stakeholders to complain if NABH or any certifying body engages in unethical practices and to approach the Ministry if such issues arise. He said the single largest focus of the Government is to eliminate corruption.
Shri Goyal concluded by reiterating that India must provide the same high-quality healthcare to every Indian patient as it provides to anyone coming from across the world. He said that just as every person wants the best healthcare for themselves and their families, it is the duty of the healthcare ecosystem to provide the same quality of healthcare to every single brother and sister from India or abroad, without discrimination between rich and poor.

title: Defence Forces given freedom & resources to respond decisively to threats: Raksha Mantri
subtitle:
“Clear distinction between peace & weakness, terror activities against India will be met with a befitting response”

India is moving forward with independent agency & strategic autonomy amid geopolitical uncertainties, says Shri Rajnath Singh

“Govt aims to make India a nation that develops advanced technologies indigenously”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 SEP 2026 8:37PM by PIB Delhi
content:
“The defence forces have been handed both freedom and resources to respond decisively to threats, including striking adversaries inside their own territory,” Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh said at an event in New Delhi on September 07, 2026. He stated that efforts were made by the adversary to undermine India’s security by all ill means including misleading the youth in Jammu & Kashmir, funding anti-India activities, spreading violence and terrorism, and attempting to create divisions within society. He asserted that the Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has foiled these nefarious designs and responded on all fronts by bringing misguided youth back into the mainstream, undertaking rehabilitation & de-radicalisation efforts, and creating employment & business opportunities.
Raksha Mantri added that Jammu and Kashmir has witnessed unprecedented progress since the abrogation of Article 370, as new avenues and opportunities have been opened up for the youth. He emphasised that India adopted the strategy of eliminating terrorism through decisive military action such as Surgical Strikes, Balakot Airstrike and Operation Sindoor, which targeted terrorists and their handlers. “The suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty sent a clear message that blood and water cannot flow together”, he said.
Shri Rajnath Singh pointed out that attempts by the adversaries to sow discord among Indians have also been successfully thwarted. Referring to the attacks that targeted places of worship during Operation Sindoor, he stated that the people of India rejected such conspiracies and demonstrated unity and social harmony.
While Raksha Mantri reiterated that India believes in peace and it does not desire war or seek to occupy the territory of any nation, he stressed that there is a clear distinction between peace and weakness. “Peace born of the fear of war is to be condemned, while war fought for the sake of peace is worthy of reverence. We’ve made it clear that if any country promotes terrorism against India, there will be no dialogue; instead, our defence forces will deliver a befitting response,” he said.
On the rapidly evolving nature of warfare, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that space and cyber space, alongside land, air and sea, have emerged as new domains of conflict, with technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, drones, autonomous systems and precision weapons transforming the battlefield. The Government is focusing on making its defence strategy and security apparatus future-ready, he said, adding that the objective is to make India a nation that develops advanced technologies indigenously.
Stating that India’s defence policy has moved beyond reactive to being pro-active, Raksha Mantri stated that it was due to PM Modi’s diplomacy and leadership that India became a member of the Missile Technology Control Regime in 2016, which facilitated efforts to extend the range of the BrahMos missile, which proved pivotal during Operation Sindoor.
On the transformation of the defence sector, Shri Rajnath Singh stressed that the Government has worked towards enhancing border security, modernising the defence forces, boosting indigenous production and revamping ordnance factories. These efforts have made the nation self-reliant and self-confident in defence, he said, underlining that defence production, which stood at around Rs 40,000 crore before 2014, has risen to approximately Rs 1.80 lakh crore, with defence exports growing 56-fold to over Rs 38,000 crore.
Raksha Mantri emphasised that India has moved from an import-dependent approach to one focused on indigenous defence manufacturing and Aatmanirbharta. “Today, our defence forces possess the indigenous Air Defence Control System ‘Akashteer’ and the next-generation air defence missile ‘Akash’. We have the Pinaka Rocket Launcher, the air-to-air missile ‘Astra’, indigenous helicopters like ‘Prachand’ and ‘Dhruv’, the ‘Tejas’ fighter aircraft, the ‘Arjun’ tank, and modern drone and counter-drone systems. Furthermore, India’s first indigenous aircraft carrier, INS Vikrant, has been inducted into the Indian Navy. We’re now producing a wide range of defence equipment while pursuing the development of sixth-generation fighter aircraft. Our aim is to export defence equipment worth Rs 50,000 crore by 2029,” he said.
Shri Rajnath Singh also highlighted the turnaround of the defence manufacturing ecosystem, stating that all 16 Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) are now operating without losses and are increasing investments in research & development and exploring new export opportunities. “Over the last 12 years, India’s defence budget has risen from Rs 2.5 lakh crore to approximately Rs 8 lakh crore, and every rupee is being utilised to strengthen India’s security with complete transparency and accountability,” he added.
Raksha Mantri pointed out that India’s security, territorial integrity and cultural identity have strengthened in the last 12 years. “India has emerged as a civilisational leader through initiatives such as International Yoga Day, revival of Nalanda University, International Solar Alliance and Global Biofuels Alliance. We’re strengthening the voice of developing nations through initiatives such as the Voice of Global South Summit and MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions). India has emerged as a reliable ‘First Responder’ to crises in neighbouring countries,” he added.
Underscoring the link between economic and national security, Shri Rajnath Singh said a strong economy is essential for developing modern military capabilities and maintaining strategic autonomy. He emphasised that despite global economic uncertainties, India is marching ahead with a growth rate of 7.8% while strengthening supply chains, promoting self-reliance in critical sectors and expanding indigenous manufacturing. He cited the development of India’s semiconductor ecosystem and the Production Linked Incentive scheme as examples of efforts to build economic resilience. “Amidst geopolitical uncertainties, many nations are being compelled to choose sides or are forced to align with specific blocs. However, India is moving forward with independent agency and strategic autonomy by focusing on its own priorities, which is why, today, when we speak, the world listens,” he said.
Elaborating on the growing participation of the private sector and MSMEs in defence production, Raksha Mantri said: “Over 16,000 MSMEs are now engaged in the sector, with defence manufacturing expanding across the country. Investment proposals worth approximately Rs 70,000 crore have been received for the Defence Industrial Corridors in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, of which nearly Rs 10,000 crore has already been invested.” He added that the efforts are being made to promote defence innovation through initiatives such as iDEX and iDEX-Prime, highlighting that the number of defence start-ups has grown from a few dozen in 2018 to more than 2,000 today.
Shri Rajnath Singh called upon the youth to become job creators and innovators, assuring the Ministry of Defence’s full support to promising ideas. He appreciated DRDO’s efforts to bring together industry, academia, start-ups and scientists to bolster Aatmanirbharta in defence. He termed the successful testing of a Scramjet Combustor in May as an important step towards hypersonic missile development. He also made special mention of the Government’s decision to transfer DRDO-developed missile technologies to Indian industry, enabling private companies to manufacture them and ensuring timely availability to the defence forces.
Raksha Mantri underlined that the Government’s objective is to achieve Aatmanirbharta in defence and create a defence ecosystem that strengthens national security, drives economic growth and enhances the country’s role in the global security architecture. He exuded confidence that by 2047, India will not only achieve the goal of Viksit Bharat, but also provide leadership to the world in technology, economy and defence.

date:

content:
The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), under the chairmanship of Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh on September 07, 2026 accorded Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) i.e., in-principle administrative approval to various acquisition proposals of the Defence Forces at an estimated cost of about Rs 1,10,000 crore. For the Indian Army, approval was granted for the procurement of Chemical Biological Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Recce Vehicles, High Mobility Vehicles (HMV), Self-Propelled Mechanical Mine Layers (MML), Advanced Light Helicopters (ALHs), Trawl Tanks and Sarvatra Bridge System.
The CBRN Recce Vehicles will be capable of detecting, identifying, monitoring and marking of areas contaminated with CBRN agents. The HMVs will enhance operational capabilities, logistic support and mobility in challenging terrains. The MMLs will achieve the desired operational capability in terms of fast and responsive minelaying in difficult terrains. The ALHs will execute complex missions across all terrains and operational situations for the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force. The Trawl Tanks and Bridge System will be utilised to provide composite crossings to fighting formations during operations in varied terrains.
For the Indian Navy, AoN was accorded for the procurement of Arudhra Radars, Design & Development and subsequent procurement of Marine Gas Turbines (MGT). Arudhra Radar will replace the existing Air Route Surveillance Radars at various Naval Air Stations and MGT, a warship propulsion system, will reduce dependency on foreign vendors.
For the Indian Air Force, approval was granted to various proposals to enhance the war-fighting capability of fighters, transports and helicopters. Approval was also accorded for procuring Ground-Based Multi-Purpose Jammer (GBMPJ) and installing Defence Forces Secure Access Card (DEFSAC) System. The GBMPJ will provide effective jamming against radars of adversaries and DEFSAC will replace existing paper based Identity Card/Passes/Permits with an interoperable Radio Frequency Identification-based smart cards system.
Of the total AoNs accorded, approximately 98% of procurements will be made from the Indian Industry.

content:
The IndiaAI Mission, under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), held a bilateral dialogue with a delegation from Sweden under the Sweden-India Technology and AI Corridor (SITAC) at Electronics Niketan, New Delhi.
The session brought together senior representatives from MeitY, IndiaAI Mission, the Embassy of Sweden in India, Business Sweden and leading Swedish companies to discuss India’s evolving AI ecosystem, digitalisation priorities and opportunities for deeper bilateral engagement in Artificial Intelligence (AI).
The session commenced with a welcome by Shri Ajit Kumar, Joint Secretary, International Cooperation Division, MeitY, followed by opening remarks by Shri Saurabh Vijay IAS, CEO, IndiaAI Mission. H.E. Agnes Julin, Minister Counsellor, Deputy Head of Mission, Embassy of Sweden in India, also addressed the gathering.
"Sweden brings deep industrial, research, and advanced manufacturing expertise, while India offers unmatched scale, digital public infrastructure, and a vast pool of AI talent and testing environments."
– Shri Saurabh Vijay IAS, CEO, IndiaAI Mission.
"With a clear roadmap focused on trade, regulation, and bridging innovative startups, our shared goal is to keep the doors wide open for business opportunities in AI and electronics between India and Sweden as we navigate this tech revolution together."
– H.E. Agnes Julin, Minister Counsellor, Deputy Head of Mission, Embassy of Sweden in India.
During the session, IndiaAI presented an overview of India’s AI ecosystem and digital roadmap, highlighting the opportunities emerging for Swedish companies across India’s rapidly expanding AI landscape. The presentation outlined the key priorities of the IndiaAI Mission, including compute capacity, datasets and models, indigenous and domain-specific AI, application development, future skills, start-up financing and Safe & Trusted AI.
The presentation also provided an overview of the opportunities emerging for international technology and industrial companies as India continues to strengthen its AI infrastructure, innovation ecosystem and pathways for responsible AI adoption.
The discussions further focused on the policy, infrastructure and governance conditions shaping enterprise AI adoption in India, including data governance, localisation, responsible AI and market access.
The Swedish delegation, led by Mr. Johnny Eriksson, Market Manager, Business Sweden, shared an overview of SITAC and Swedish priorities in AI and digitalisation. Representatives from leading Swedish companies including Autoliv, Consat, IKEA, Saab, Sandvik AI, Sandvik Intelligent Manufacturing, SKF and Volvo Group participated in the discussions.
The interactive dialogue brought together leading Swedish companies and representatives from India’s AI and technology ecosystem, including Tech Mahindra, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Zenteiq, Avataar AI, Innefu, CoRover.ai, Gnani and Globals ITES. The discussion explored potential areas of convergence between Swedish industrial and technology capabilities and India’s AI priorities, including industrial AI, trusted data, compute, skills and responsible AI, with an emphasis on translating areas of shared interest into practical engagement.
The participation of Indian AI and technology companies provided the Swedish delegation with an opportunity to gain insights into India’s enterprise AI capabilities, technology solutions and deployment-ready innovations. The interaction also sought to identify opportunities for pilots, co-development, commercial partnerships and other forms of industry engagement based on specific enterprise and industrial requirements.
The discussions under SITAC are expected to contribute towards a focused and sustained Sweden–India engagement agenda in AI and digitalisation, including potential pilots, testbeds, ecosystem partnerships and other avenues for continued cooperation.
The session concluded with a vote of thanks by Mr. Johnny Eriksson, Market Manager, Business Sweden, followed by closing remarks from the IndiaAI Mission.
The bilateral dialogue reflects the shared interest of India and Sweden in leveraging AI and emerging technologies to strengthen innovation, enterprise adoption and technology-led growth, while fostering responsible and trusted AI ecosystems.

India and the US Discuss Strengthening Cooperation across Semiconductors, AI and Data Centres and Advancing Technology-Led Opportunities

Hon’ble MoS visits Duke University, Engages with Leadership and Researchers and Explores Opportunities for Collaboration in AI, Robotics, Innovation and Emerging Technologies
date:

                07 SEP 2026 5:08PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Hon’ble Union Minister of State (MoS) for Electronics & Information Technology and Commerce & Industry, Shri Jitin Prasada, led the Indian delegation at the G20 Innovation Ministers’ Meeting held on 1–2 September 2026 in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, United States (US), hosted by the US Department of Commerce and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP). The Hon’ble MoS was accompanied by Shri Ajit Kumar, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), senior officials from MeitY,Department of Science and Technology (DST) and Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), as well as officials of the Embassy of India in the US.
At the conclusion of the Ministerial, the G20 Ministers released the Innovation Ministerial Statement recognizing that “emerging technologies have the potential to unlock prosperity, enhance productivity, and expand opportunity for all our peoples.”
The consensus statement articulates shared broad agreement across six pillars: pro-innovation policy frameworks, technology for opportunity and prosperity, skilled technical workforce development, intellectual property policies for artificial intelligence (AI), AI for standards and standards for AI, and industrial innovation and investment in supply chains. Ministers also reached consensus on the Carolina Principles for Emerging Technologies
,
which call on countries to invest in foundational research, strengthen commercialization pathways, and enable trusted technology adoption and deployment. Other deliverables of the Ministerial included the AI Prosperity Objectives and the AI Prosperity Compact, which will further technical workforce development across G20 nations and expand opportunities for private sector partnership.
On the sidelines of the G20 Ministerial, Hon’ble MoS held several bilateral discussions.
In his bilateral meeting with H.E. Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President of the European Commission, both discussed the importance of strengthening cooperation in innovation and building trusted digital ecosystems that enable technology-led growth and shared prosperity.
In the meeting with H.E. Anne Le Hénanff, Minister Delegate for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Affairs of France, both sides discussed advancing cooperation in AI and digital technologies. India and France remain committed to strengthening technology-driven innovation and building partnerships for a trusted digital future.
During the meeting with H.E. Thomas Jarzombek and H.E. Dr. Silke Launert, Parliamentary State Secretaries, Germany, Hon’ble MoS explored opportunities to further deepen India–Germany collaboration in technology, innovation and research, driving shared progress and future-ready partnerships.
In discussions with H.E. Prof. Gaspard Banyankimbona, Commissioner for Education, Science, Technology and Innovation, African Union, the commitment to deepening partnership with Africa and creating new opportunities for shared growth and prosperity was highlighted by offering India Stack digital solutions including DPI to the African countries.
In the bilateral discussion with H.E. Howard Lutnick, US Secretary of Commerce, both sides exchanged views on strengthening cooperation across Semiconductors, AI and Data Centres. During the meeting, Hon’ble MoS also encouraged the possibility of more US investments in ISM2.0, proposed strengthening AI technology partnership and shared mechanism for safeguards for AI.
Hon’ble MoS also engaged with Tom Brown, Co-founder of Anthropic, and discussed the rapidly evolving AI landscape and opportunities emerging from advances in AI. Some key discussions included the possibility of collaboration to develop benchmarks for the Indian context.
Hon’ble MoS during Duke University Visit
Following the G20 engagements, the Hon’ble MoS visited Duke University, where he interacted with the senior leadership and faculty to exchange views on areas of mutual interest, including technology, research, engineering, artificial intelligence, computer science and healthcare. The visit also included a tour of the Robotics Laboratory at the Pratt School of Engineering, where the Hon’ble MoS engaged with leading researchers and experts working at the intersection of robotics, biomedical simulation, AI-enabled sensing and biomedical data, and machine learning. The interactions underscored the significant potential for deepening academic and research collaboration between India and the United States in emerging and transformative technologies.
The engagements during the visit underscored India’s growing role in shaping the global technology and innovation agenda and reaffirmed its commitment to building strategic partnerships that translate advances in AI, semiconductors, DPI, robotics and other emerging technologies into greater opportunities for innovation, economic growth and an improved quality of life for its citizens.

Hosted by the National Internet Exchange of India (NIXI) and the Internet Service Providers Association of India (ISPAI) with the support of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and Government of Maharashtra, APNIC 62 is organized by the Asia Pacific Network Information Centre (APNIC), the region’s not-for-profit Internet number registry.
The event will bring together technical experts, network operators, policymakers and leaders from the Internet community to examine some of the most significant challenges and opportunities shaping the Internet’s future. This includes AI-powered services, network automation, cybersecurity, routing security and Internet governance issues.
“As India’s digital ecosystem continues to expand, ensuring secure, resilient and future-ready Internet infrastructure remains a key priority. APNIC 62 provides an important platform for India to engage with the Asia Pacific technical community, exchanging knowledge and strengthening collaboration towards an open, inclusive and trusted Internet for all,” says Shri Sushil Pal, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
Distinguished guests will include Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India and Shri Rajesh Aggarwal, Chief Secretary of the Government of Maharashtra.
“AI and other major technical and societal shifts are placing unprecedented demands on the networks that underpin our economies and societies. APNIC 62 brings the region’s Internet community together to turn shared expertise into practical action for a more secure, resilient and scalable Internet,” says APNIC Director General Jia Rong Low.
Low adds: “India’s leadership in IPv6 adoption shows what is possible when technical capability, investment and collaboration align. Mumbai is a natural place to bring together the Asia Pacific Internet community to share that experience and help plan for the Internet’s continued growth.”
“NIXI is proud to host APNIC 62 in Mumbai at a time when India’s digital economy and Internet infrastructure are growing rapidly. APNIC 62 is an opportunity to share India’s experience, learn from regional experts and strengthen the cooperation needed for a secure, resilient and inclusive Internet,” says Dr. Devesh Tyagi, Chief Executive Officer, NIXI.
“India’s Internet service providers are at the frontline of meeting rapidly growing demand for reliable, secure and high-performing connectivity. APNIC 62 gives operators from across the Asia Pacific an important opportunity to share practical experience, strengthen technical cooperation and prepare their networks for what comes next,” says Rajesh Chharia, President of ISPAI.
The Opening Ceremony will feature keynotes from Lightstorm Group CEO and Managing Director Amajit Gupta on AI-driven network automation, and JPCERT/CC’s Yukako Uchida on the role of trust and cooperation in cybersecurity.
On 8 September, at the sidelines of APNIC 62, NIXI and APNIC will sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to enhance the deployment of key Internet infrastructure technologies – IPv6 and routing security, which will contribute to the
strengthening of the security, resilience, and long-term development of India's Internet infrastructure.
About APNIC 62
APNIC 62 runs from 4 to 10 September 2026 in Mumbai, with technical workshops, conference sessions, policy meetings and community events focused on a secure and resilient Internet in the Asia Pacific.
About APNIC
APNIC, the Asia Pacific Network Information Centre, is one of the quiet enablers of the global Internet.
Behind every website load, video stream, or AI powered service is a set of shared technical resources that allow networks to find and connect with each other. APNIC helps manage those critical resources
-
Internet addresses and network identifiers
-
across 56 economies in the Asia Pacific region.
From major global providers to small community networks, APNIC works with thousands of organizations to ensure the Internet can continue to grow safely and reliably. Its role is not regulatory or political, but technical: helping the Internet function as a single, interoperable system across borders.
In simple terms, APNIC helps make sure the Internet works
-
not just today, but for the long term
-
supporting an open, stable, and secure digital future for the Asia Pacific region.
